findings.title: CTF Flag - SSRF via file:// scheme bypasses admin restriction
findings.description: The Markdown-to-HTML converter at /convert accepts a URL parameter and uses Python's urllib.request.urlopen() to fetch the content. urllib supports the file:// scheme, enabling Local File Read / SSRF. The admin restriction at /admin and /admin/flag checks request.remote_addr == '127.0.0.1', but the file:// scheme bypasses the need to make an HTTP request entirely - it reads local files directly. The FLAG is hardcoded in app.py and was read using: url=file:///proc/self/cwd/app.py

reproduction.expected: Returns app source code containing FLAG = "flag{cbf59a8d-b5f1-4a8e-8286-0c249b14d682}"

diagrams.title: Markdown Converter App - Attack Surface
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
    Attacker["Attacker"] --> Convert["POST /convert\n(URL or markdown_text)"]
    Attacker --> Admin["GET /admin\n403 Forbidden from external"]
    Attacker --> AdminFlag["GET /admin/flag\n403 Forbidden from external"]
    Convert --> urllib["urllib.request.urlopen(url)"]
    urllib --> FileRead["file:///proc/self/cwd/app.py\nLFI via file:// scheme"]
    urllib --> SSRF["http://127.0.0.1:55561/admin\nBlocked by URL filter"]
    FileRead --> FLAG["FLAG extracted from app.py\nflag{cbf59a8d-b5f1-4a8e-8286-0c249b14d682}"]
    Admin --> AdminCheck["request.remote_addr == 127.0.0.1?"]
    AdminFlag --> AdminCheck
    AdminCheck --> |"Yes - localhost"| FlagTemplate["flag.html rendered"]
    AdminCheck --> |"No - external"| Forbidden["403 Forbidden"]
